text: 🔥🇲🇽 "It would be worth it for the Bank of Mexico to do a review." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 Contralínea listed lifetime Bank of Mexico pensions above the President's salary, which the Constitution sets as the cap for public servants: 150,000 pesos a month for ex-president Ernesto Zedillo, 330,000 for Guillermo Ortiz, 350,000 for Francisco Gil Díaz, 412,000 for Miguel Mancera Aguayo. The golden pensions reform caps payouts at CFE, Nafinsa, Banobras and other federal bodies, but the central bank was left out. Some of those officials worked only six years at the bank. Sheinbaum said this is not about workers' pensions, only those of governors and deputy governors, and Zedillo was neither.

🚨🇲🇽 "In Mexico, it is necessarily the people who must decide." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 Contralínea asked about the network of Fernando Cerimedo, now on trial in Bolivia, and his partner Javier Negre. The outlet has linked it to the PRI leadership, Claudio X. González's Sí por México, and Dick Morris, who worked on the 2006 "danger to Mexico" campaign against López Obrador. Sheinbaum described how the network operates: their outlet La Derecha Diaria publishes mostly false news, they buy accounts with large followings, and they pay for AI-driven bots that feed the algorithms. Under Mexican law, an election can be annulled if foreign intervention that changed the result is proven.

🚨🇲🇽 "It can't be that one talks about the rule of law and then, when push comes to shove, doesn't meet the requirements." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 Sheinbaum laid out the law on Querétaro's new international police academy, where the US ambassador laid the first stone. Article 117 of the Constitution bars states from making alliances or treaties with foreign powers. Any foreign security cooperation with a state needs approval from the federal high-level security group and the Foreign Ministry. Querétaro has nine such projects with US law enforcement agencies, approved since 2021. The academy is not one of them, even though Querétaro's security secretary said at the event that it is designed to receive training from US agencies. "Why? Because it is the law."

🇲🇽✊ "I had practically nothing. I slept on the floor with my children." — Olga Lidia Rodríguez, Vivienda para el Bienestar beneficiary, Lerdo, Durango Olga is a single mother of four who earns the minimum wage and spent six years moving from rental to rental. Today she received her own home in Lerdo, Durango, one of 303 delivered there. The Vivienda para el Bienestar program has now placed 44,000 homes in 27 states, with eight more developments opening in October. In Durango alone, the 25,000-home goal means 15 billion pesos of investment and about 100,000 jobs, according to Governor Esteban Villegas.

🇲🇽✊ "The fundamental rule of the medical model is zero rejections." — Alejandro Svarch, director of IMSS-Bienestar From January 2027, 12,750 primary care clinics will open in the 24 states that joined IMSS-Bienestar. Anyone can walk in, whether they have IMSS, ISSSTE, Pemex or no coverage at all. Care will be free, with 60 basic medicines. Mexico's health system has been fragmented since 1943; this is the first step toward universal service. Neighborhood committees will receive the funds to fix up each site. Since September 14, 73,000 doctors and nurses have applied to staff them, and retired ones can join without losing their pension.

🇲🇽✊ "It is a government that doesn't wait for people to come, but goes out to meet them and knocks on the door of their home." — Leticia Ramírez, Secretary of Well-being Salud Casa por Casa has made more than 27 million free home medical visits to older adults and people with disabilities who receive well-being pensions. Health workers have knocked on 10 million doors, and 8.3 million people have had a second visit. Patients found with uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes are referred to IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar or Pemex: more than 850,000 for hypertension and 225,000 for diabetes so far. Nurses have handled over 45,000 emergencies.

text: 🇲🇽🔍 "They were carrying out an operation on the ground." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 Asked about the CIA's undisclosed operations in Chihuahua, where two US agents died, Sheinbaum said the Attorney General's Office still has the investigation open and has to report its progress. "One must always lament the loss of lives, but they were carrying out an operation on the ground." Any state government that wants a security relationship with a US agency, or any foreign government, has to go through the high-level security group and get authorization from the Foreign Ministry.
